To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed integrated concurrency control method is effective and efficient in the joint scheduling and management of soft real-time and traditional non-real-time database applications.
the performance of nonreal-time transactions can be significantly degraded by real-time transactions if the real-time support is not properly designed.
the performance of nonreal-time transactions in mixed soft real time database systems is highly affected by the concurrency control strategies used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three issues: (1) The design of an effective and practical concurrency control method for soft real-time databases.

the concurrency control problems for mixed soft real time database systems, in particular, the impacts of soft real-time support on the non-real-time transaction performance and the tradeoff between cost and performance in the design of concurrency control protocols.

the following issues: 1. How to design cost-effective concurrency control protocols to support soft real-time transactions; 2. How to minimize the impact of soft real-time transaction support on non-real-time transaction performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a mixed real-time database system with a real-time scheduler and a two phase locking concurrency control protocol is a better choice than one with a non-real-time scheduler and an optimistic concurrency control protocol.
the performance of the integrated protocols is better than that of the original protocols in both the real-time and non real-time environments.

a cost effective concurrency control strategy for mixed soft real time database systems should be a hybrid of two phase locking and time stamping with the following features: a) the time stamping is only used to support soft real-time transactions; b) the time stamp value of a soft real-time transaction is determined by its deadline; and c) the time stamp is not updated when a transaction commits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the performance of non real-time transactions is significantly affected by the scheduling approach of real-time transactions, and the performance of real-time transactions is also affected by the concurrency control method used.

the performance tradeoff between soft real-time and traditional non-real-time transactions is very significant and the performance of nonreal-time transactions could be greatly degraded if we only consider the real-time requirements of soft real time transactions.

, in general, the two-phase locking method is more suitable for soft real-time transaction processing, and the optimistic concurrency control method should be applied to non-real-time transactions, while the combination of these two methods can provide an efficient and cost-effective solution to mixed soft real-time systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to design a cost-effective concurrency control method that can meet the deadline requirement of soft real-time applications while minimizing the performance impact of soft real-time concurrency control on non-real-time transactions.
the performance of soft real-time and hard real-time database systems can be improved by integrating concurrency control techniques with the scheduling of soft real-time database transactions.
, for mixed soft real time database systems, the performance of nonreal-time transactions is significantly affected by the real-time support in the system.
